question: Should experimental Claw lifecycle ownership become a core doctor contract now, and if so must diagnostics preserve a strict zero-directory-mutation guarantee for WAL databases?
rationale: The open RFC and stacked ownership work define a new core lifecycle and persistent-state contract; automation cannot decide whether sidecar creation is acceptable or whether the feature should wait for the stack to stabilize.

options.title: Require strict read-only proof
options.body: Sponsor the core diagnostic only after the opener and tests guarantee no database or sidecar directory mutation and real CLI proof is posted.

options.title: Accept SQLite sidecars
options.body: Explicitly narrow the contract so advisory diagnostics may create SQLite-maintained sidecars while never changing logical database contents.

options.title: Pause for the RFC stack
options.body: Keep this draft pending until the RFC and prerequisite ownership PRs establish the permanent lifecycle and storage boundary.

recommendation.title: Require strict read-only proof
recommendation.body: Sponsor the core diagnostic only after the opener and tests guarantee no database or sidecar directory mutation and real CLI proof is posted.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to the merged Claws history, were explicitly mentioned on this PR, and are the strongest available owner for the core product-contract choice.
